about: ERRATA 105: the everyday sounds, wired. Every cue is doc 45's, by its id, and plays a file Tyler approved by ear (errata 102). Footsteps follow the floor: a walk box whose own `surface` is boardwalk walks on boards; anywhere else the room's floor below. Nothing here marks a load-bearing LISTEN: the timesheet's paper is the same ordinary paper as the queue book's (doc 45 R08-TIME, section 3.5). ERRATA 106 adds the opening's cues (Tyler reversed errata 28a's ban on timed sound), the remaining LISTEN cues, the stamp and the judges' pencil, and the room backgrounds.

R23/24-MUD.why: doc 45 R23/24-MUD: a localized wet working, squelching

U-STAMP.why: doc 45 U-STAMP: a stamp landing on paper, where the writing says one does Errata 149: Tyler's pick by ear, "B · Ink pad, then stamp"; gain as he heard it.

S6-SEAL.why: Doc 48 S6 beat 3: "The county seal comes down. One stamp. It is the loudest sound in the game and the score rests under it." The rendered seal (tools/audio/render-seal-sfx.py, errata 99 P), now a cue (errata 106 reverses 28a's ban on timed sound for cues): the music ducks under it for the stamp and its tail and comes back. The loudest effect in the game on purpose: `levels.loudest` names it, and tools/check-sound-levels.mjs holds it 6 dB over every other sound.

U-ASSAY-PENCIL.why: doc 45 U-ASSAY-PENCIL: the judges' pencil, each point written down (doc 03: Sowerby holds it)

R17-BELL.why: doc 45 R17-BELL: pulling the rope strikes the bell -- the same fixed, half-step-flat bell heard from Main Street, here directly overhead. Doc 49's PULL line has always been in the game; it had no sound. Errata 108: a pull swings the bell, so it tolls -- three strikes, ringing out over twelve seconds -- with the music dipped before the first strike lands.

LIV-HUM.why: doc 04 LIV_A1 option 4's staging: "He hums the pitch. Badly. It is recognisably the town theme and recognisably wrong, and Thad's ear files it." The town theme's first phrase, hummed off (errata 109).

B3-WHISTLE.why: doc 02 B3: Grievance responds to one whistled pitch, and Thad, by ear, corrects it. The fork, the phrase whistled right, and she goes (errata 109). Errata 197: sounded from doc 95's act (row 79) as the staging plays, not at the click, and her steps come after the long moment; the music comes back with the look (a dip held through silence is a hole).

A-TUNING.why: doc 02 A2 and A8: the piano tuned. The flat C-sharp as the room has always heard it, the fork, the pin turning, and the same notes mended (errata 109).

FID-FASTER.why: Doc 07 #11, the fiddler's R_BORDERS_MOTT bark: "He plays something faster. Still flat." CONSOLATION's tune, once through, at half again the speed (errata 116).

FID-PASSING.why: Doc 07 #11, the fiddler's R_DEAD bark: "He plays the passing tune. Correctly. Flat." The funeral's arrangement, slow and a half step down to the bell, its first half (errata 116).

R33-FIDDLER.why: Doc 07 #11 R_TRUTH: "In F2, twenty seconds into the tuning arc, he stops mid-phrase, tunes his A, and continues. He is the only character in Consolation who notices anything, and it is never remarked upon." Doc 06: "The fiddler in the Nugget corrects first, about twenty seconds in." Far off, under the score, off the music bus so it is in tune while the score is not (errata 116).

F4-ERUPTS.why: doc 03 Duel Four: "The street erupts." Errata 131 E: the town roars on the line after Sowerby's verdict, over the silence that held before it (the music stays down until the duel is over). Errata 149: Tyler's pick by ear, "B · Cheering"; gain as he heard it.

F4-DOOR.why: doc 03 Duel Four: "He walks back up the street to his office, and for the first time in twelve years, he closes the door." Errata 131 F: the approved latch, off the frame, once Fanshawe has gone.

BR-STRIKE.why: Doc 07 #4, the bell-ringer: 'Strikes the bell by hand, half a step flat.' His idle strike on Lower Street (errata 161): the town's flat bell, near, once, timed to the frame the mallet lands (the break's third step, 0.68 s in). A background sound, not a remark: no duck.

BR-STRIKE-ONE.why: Doc 07 #4's bark '(strikes)': one blow on the bell as Thad comes up, the bark itself (errata 161).

BR-STRIKE-HALF.why: Doc 07 #4, R_LOST_DUEL: '(strikes, half-heartedly)': one blow, softer (errata 161).

BR-STRIKE-FOUR.why: Doc 07 #4, R_WON_DUEL: '(strikes four times, unasked, at eleven at night)' (errata 161).

BR-PASSING.why: Doc 07 #4, R_DEAD: 'He rings the passing bell.' The slow toll the church's rope rings (R17-BELL's file), three strokes over twelve seconds (errata 161).

R52-FORK.why: doc 45 R52-FORK: USE THE TUNING FORK on the fiddle (G5) -- the fork, exact A440, off the bus, then the pegs turning (tools/audio/render-gulch-sfx.py).

R52-FIDDLE.why: doc 45 R52-FIDDLE: the rule-keeper plays, very badly and very happily, a few seconds, no theme; on the bus, since it is an instrument, with R52-M ducked under it (errata 107).

R53-PEBBLE.why: doc 45 R53-PEBBLE: the rule-keeper moves a pebble from one pile to the other after each exchange of Duel One on the bar -- one pebble set down on gravel, cold, its natural tail (doc 109; tools/audio/render-gulch-sfx.py). In place of the judges' pencil, heard over the jaw harp at a featured cue's level.

lines.line: He notarizes it. He stamps it. He does not look up.
That's what the fella whistled. Twelve years I've been getting it wrong.

levels.about: TYLER, 2026-11-06: "make sure sfx aren't absurdly loud ... background effects not sounds that take center stage." Targets in dB against the median room bed (the music as it plays), and the gains in this file are set from them by measurement, never by ear alone. tools/check-sound-levels.mjs fails on any sound above its ceiling, which is the target plus 2 dB. `roomGain` turns a room's own scripted sounds down together -- the coffin's dirt and the chamber's taps -- whose loudest must sit no higher than the music (`scene`, 0 dB): in the coffin there is no music, and those sounds are the room, but not a slap. The two synthesized human sounds -- the Nugget's talk and the distant laugh -- sit lower than their kinds (20 and 16 dB under), because a voice made by synthesis is most convincing when it is barely there (errata 106). A cue with a `duck` dips the music under it, and its target is measured against its own room's music as ducked rather than the median: the bells (Tyler: "The bell is hard to hear over the music") ring over a dipped score, the near one 6 dB above it, the distant one 2. ERRATA 122 (Tyler, 2026-11-06, listening to every room at its real level: "you can't hear really any of the background sounds and noises. The music completely overpowers everything."): the places were set too low, 16-20 dB under the score. Backgrounds now sit 8 under (the Nugget's synthesized crowd 12), their layers 10, footsteps 10 (the loudest step of each floor), one-offs 4, and every per-cue place 6 higher than it was; the featured moments, the Strike and the tuning arc's fiddler keep their places. The check now has a floor as well as a ceiling: no place lower than -12, and no sound more than 6 dB under its place. The coffin's and the chamber's scripted sounds keep a ceiling only: their distance is the scene. The Nugget's crowd and the registrar's bed were re-rendered nearer full scale (tools/audio/render-room-sfx.py) so their gains stay under 1. ERRATA 148: U-STAMP's place is -10, measured on the 400 ms window: the stamp Tyler chose by ear is a short dab and thump, quieter on that window than the old ringing one at the same peak, and it is set at the level he heard and picked.
levels.cueBedsNote: Tyler, 2026-11-07, of the opening under the stars: "I didn't hear horses." The halted team sat at the beds' -8, twelve under the fiddle in Room 1; it is the only sound in the dark before anyone speaks, and is placed at -2.

loudest.note: Doc 48 S6 beat 3: "It is the loudest sound in the game." The one named exception to errata 106's places: its own place is set over its ducked room like any cue's, and tools/check-sound-levels.mjs also holds that, against the music, it is at least `overNext` dB louder than any other sound in the game. Nothing else may be named here.
